GazeNeRF is a 3D-aware method for gaze redirection that reformulates the task as a neural volume rendering problem [12127-gazenerf.md].
It solves the limitation of existing 2D methods by explicitly modeling the rigid 3D rotation of eyeballs and the non-rigid deformation of the face separately [12127-gazenerf.md].

Unlike sibling methods that mix facial features or lack 3D consistency, GazeNeRF uses a two-stream MLP architecture to predict volumetric features for the face (excluding eyes) and eyes independently, applying a rigid 3D rotation matrix to the eye features before compositing [12127-gazenerf.md].
HeadNeRF is a parametric head model that integrates neural radiance fields (NeRF) into the parametric representation of the human head to render high-fidelity images in real-time [12332-headnerf.md].

It solves the problem of computationally expensive NeRF rendering by decoupling geometry and appearance prediction and employing a 2D neural rendering module, allowing direct control over rendering pose and semantic attributes (identity, expression, albedo, illumination) [12332-headnerf.md].

Unlike standard NeRF which predicts color directly from 3D coordinates and viewing direction, HeadNeRF predicts a high-dimensional feature vector and density, removing the viewing direction input to mitigate dataset bias [12332-headnerf.md].
Since ray direction and point distance are undefined in the undirected volume, exploit uniform voxel distribution to cancel constant $\delta_t$.
